message.content:
Based on my search, here are the main ways to pay your federal taxes online:

## Official IRS Online Payment Options

### 1. **IRS Direct Pay** (Recommended for most individuals)
- **Website**: directpay.irs.gov
- **Cost**: Free - no fees
- **How it works**: Pay directly from your U.S. checking or savings account
- **Features**: 
  - No registration required (guest access)
  - Schedule payments up to 365 days in advance
  - Same-day payment option available
  - Change or cancel up to 2 business days before payment date
  - Available Monday-Saturday (midnight to 11:45 p.m. EST) and Sunday (7 a.m. to 11:45 p.m. EST)
- **Limitations**: Maximum 2 payments per day; cannot use international bank accounts

### 2. **IRS Online Account**
- **Cost**: Free for ACH bank transfers
- **Features**: View your balance, payment history, make payments, and manage payment plans
- **Requires**: ID-verified account registration

### 3. **Debit or Credit Card**
- **Processors**: Pay1040 or ACI Payments, Inc.
- **Fees**: 
  - Debit card: ~$2.10-$2.15 flat fee
  - Credit card: 1.75%-1.85% of payment amount (minimum $2.50)
- **Note**: The IRS does not charge the fee - it goes to the payment processor

### 4. **Electronic Funds Withdrawal (EFW)**
- **When**: Available when e-filing through tax software, tax professional, or IRS Free File
- **Cost**: Generally free (check with your bank for any fees)
- **Features**: Schedule payments up to 365 days in advance

### 5. **Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS)**
- **Website**: eftps.gov
- **Important Update**: As of October 17, 2025, EFTPS **stopped accepting new individual enrollments**. Existing users can continue using it.
- **Still available for**: Business taxpayers, federal agencies, and individuals enrolled before the cutoff date

### 6. **IRS2Go Mobile App**
- **Cost**: Free app
- **Features**: Make payments via mobile version of Direct Pay (free) or by debit/credit card (with fees)

## Important Recent Change

An **Executive Order signed March 25, 2025** requires federal tax payments to be made electronically. Paper checks and money orders will no longer be accepted after **September 30, 2025**. This affects:
- Federal estimated tax payments due January 15, 2026 and beyond
- All other federal tax payments after September 30, 2025

Exceptions apply for individuals without banking access, emergency situations, and other legal exemptions.

## How to Choose

| If you want... | Use this method |
|---------------|-----------------|
| Free, simple, no registration | IRS Direct Pay |
| Account management & history | IRS Online Account |
| Fast payment with card rewards | Debit/Credit Card |
| Pay while e-filing | Electronic Funds Withdrawal |
| Business/payroll taxes | EFTPS (if already enrolled) or Direct Pay |

Sources:
1. https://turbotax.intuit.com/tax-tips/tax-payments/how-to-pay-taxes-10-ways-to-pay-your-tax-bill/L6CR274jr
2. https://fiscal.treasury.gov/payments-to-government/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system-eftps
3. https://www.taxesforexpats.com/articles/expat-tax-rules/how-to-pay-taxes-online.html
4. https://www.nerdwallet.com/taxes/learn/pay-irs-options
5. https://www.zinnerco.com/zinner-blog/executive-order-requires-electronic-payment-of-federal-tax
6. https://www.taxbuddy.com/blog/advance-tax-payment-online
7. https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nasir-ahmed-922b342a5_usa-payroll-tax-payment-to-irs-using-quickbooks-activity-7265717672586153986-KKR3
8. https://www.tax1099.com/irs/irs-federal-tax-payment/
